messages.subject: ggplot2 book
parts:

messages.author: 52e73b2030a3e651
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 book
parts:
It has been out for a while -- please consider using the link from the webpage --

http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/book/

as this will cause more of the book's purchase price to accrue to Hadley without costing the buyer any more.  (At some point Hadley mentioned that this effectively doubles the share of proceeds which end up in his bank account -- not bad for $0.00 extra :-))

I had the full PDF and bought the book anyways; I could not do most of my work effectively without ggplot2 (and rgl and rpanel, but that is another story for another day).  Another package which may be of interest to biological investigators is the NeatMap package, which recently appeared in a BMC Bioinformatics article and uses ggplot2 extensively.

http://www.biomedcentral.com/1471-2105/11/45

And just the other day, someone wrote a package implementing Tamara Munzner's hyperbolic geometry for tree and graph visualization in R: 

http://fisheyer.r-forge.r-project.org/

I don't know if there has ever been a better time to work on data visualization.
